title: Misir Wat
subtitle: Ethiopian spiced red lentils
excerpt: Misir wat is a thick, deeply spiced red lentil stew that is a staple across Ethiopian cuisine. The long cook time lets the spices meld into something far more complex than the ingredient list suggests.
sourceNotes: Misir wat is a staple Ethiopian dish traditionally seasoned with berbere, a complex spice blend. This version approximates the berbere flavour using individual spices that are easier to source.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the batch and freeze half.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Misir wat deepens in flavour overnight. It keeps refrigerated for up to 4 days.

content.text: Misir wat gets its depth from two things: a long, slow cook of the onions until they are almost jammy, and a spice mix that leans heavily on warmth rather than heat. The onions are not browned quickly here; they are coaxed down over a low hob for 15 to 20 minutes until soft and sweet. This is the base that carries everything else.

Traditional Ethiopian berbere includes fenugreek and other spices not listed here. The spices below give a similar warmth without specialist ingredients. If you have a shop-bought berbere blend, use 2 tablespoons instead of the cumin, coriander, paprika, cinnamon, and chilli flakes.

Heat the oil in a large saucepan over a low-medium hob. Add the diced onion with a pinch of salt and cook, stirring occasionally, for 15 to 20 minutes until the onion is very soft, pale golden, and reduced in volume by roughly half.
Add the garlic and ginger. Stir and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant. Add the tomato puree and cook for a further 2 minutes, stirring constantly so it does not catch.
Add all the ground spices: cumin, coriander, smoked paprika, chilli flakes, turmeric, and cinnamon. Stir well and cook for 1 minute until the spices smell toasted and the mixture is very fragrant.
Pour in the tinned tomatoes and 400 ml of water. Stir, scraping any bits from the base of the pan. Add the rinsed red lentils and stir again.

Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low. Simmer uncovered for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until the lentils have completely broken down and the stew is thick. Add a splash of water if it becomes too dry before the lentils are cooked through.
Season well with salt. Serve with flatbread or rice, and a wedge of lemon or lime on the side if you have one.

items.symptom: The lentils are still gritty after 25 minutes
items.cause: The heat was too high, evaporating the liquid before the lentils had time to cook through fully.
items.fix: Add 100 ml of water, reduce the heat to the lowest setting, put a lid on the pan, and continue cooking for another 10 minutes.

items.symptom: The wat has caught on the base of the pan
items.cause: Red lentils are starchy and will stick if left without stirring, especially in the final stages when the mixture is thick.
items.fix: Stir every 5 minutes and keep the heat low. Use a heavy-based pan to distribute heat more evenly.

items.symptom: The flavour is flat despite all the spices
items.cause: The spices were not toasted in the oil long enough before the liquid went in, so they did not bloom properly.
items.fix: Season assertively with salt at the end: lentil dishes often need more than you expect. A squeeze of lemon also brightens the overall flavour considerably.
